screens.name: ROM check screen (A+B at power-on)
screens.how_shown: Hold A and B on controller 1 at power-on/reset: S_8510 ($8064) sees $07 & $C0 == $C0 and runs the PRG sum ($8523-$8552) and the CHR check (bank 3), then prints "KONAMI ONE/TEN" and "GRADIUS ONE/TEN" on a grey screen.
screens.notes: Both checks pass on the supplied ROMs.

screens.name: Title screen
screens.how_shown: After power-on: mode $00=0 builds it (sub 1: the screen scrolls in from the right, $12 from $FE down by 2 per frame, frames 6-134), mode 1 waits for START/SELECT (cursor = Vic Viper sprite, metasprite 1 at Y $86/$96, S_82A1). The attract demo starts at frame 391 if nothing is pressed.

screens.name: Attract demo
screens.how_shown: Mode 2 after 257 idle frames on the title (frames 391-3631 in usE): stage 1 played by the program with equipment; returns to the title (mode 0).
screens.notes: Every attract cycle in usE (3 cycles) played stage 1.

screens.name: Stage start / respawn
screens.how_shown: $1B = $01..$04 at each stage start and after each death: screen blank while the HUD (block 28/15) and palettes (block 16 + the stage tail 8-14) are queued, then $1B=$80 play. No stage title is shown.

screens.name: Pause
screens.how_shown: START during play toggles $15; the picture freezes, no overlay or text. The Konami code (UP UP DOWN DOWN LEFT RIGHT LEFT RIGHT B A, sequence $9793 checked by S_9765 with X=2) entered while paused gives speed, missile, 2 options and shield.

screens.name: Game over
screens.how_shown: $1B=$C0 after the last life: HUD row 28 shows "1P  GAME OVER" (or "2P"), about 400 frames, then mode 0 (title). Text in the status-bar font (CHR bank 1).

screens.name: Continue (code at game over)
screens.how_shown: During the game-over screen enter DOWN UP B A B A B A B A (sequence $9789, S_9765 X=0, counter $33). When the timer $4C ends with $33 == 10 ($9715-$9746) the player gets 3 lives, score reset, and restarts the stage. No dedicated screen: the stage-start sequence follows.

screens.name: Two-player alternation
screens.how_shown: Title "2 PLAYERS" (SELECT then START): $18 = current player, HUD row 29 shows "1P"/"2P"; players alternate after each death; "1P/2P GAME OVER" in the HUD.

screens.name: Secret stage skip (warp)
screens.how_shown: At a stage end with the flag $39 set ($9935-$9945: INC $19, INC $3A, $1B=$8E) the next stage is skipped: state $8E/$8F selects CHR bank 2 ($984F), scrolls 4 px per frame and shows outline Moai sprites (type 38) until $3F >= $11. $39 is set by: 4 hatches destroyed in stage 1 with an even score digit ($AF67-$AF7E), a quick kill of the stage-2 Big Core ($04CC == 1 and $04AC < $78, $B962-$B978), or 10 Moai heads destroyed ($5F >= 10, $C77C-$C786). Seen in usB/usL2 (stage 3 -> stage 5): there $5F reached 10 because the invincible (patched) ship rammed the Moai mouths, which counts as hits.

screens.name: Ending (US)
screens.how_shown: After stage 7 ($1B $87->$88..$8D): starfield with the mothership (metasprite $9E, slot $14) and the Vic Viper approaching (type 40, metasprites $96-$9D), then "CONGRATULATIONS!" typed one letter per 9 frames at $22C8, then loop 2 starts at stage 1 ($1A+1). Same message on every loop: the pointer table $CF2D holds 7 x $CF3B.
screens.notes: usL2 f115064 (loop 2) shows the same text.

screens.name: Ending (JP, six messages)
screens.how_shown: Same sequence as the US ending, but the text shows "BONUS 100000", one of six messages chosen by the loop number (JP pointer table $CF05 -> $CF28..$CF6D: KANGEKI!, OMIGOTO!, NIKUI NIKUI!, ANTAWA SUGOI!, MIAGETAMONDA!, IUKOTONAINE! - initials K O N A M I) and "LET'S GO NEXT ZONE" ($CF12 at $2306).
screens.notes: Loop 6 also shows a stray "O" tile at row 18 under the bonus line (jpEnd f388220).

gaps.what: Metasprites $09, $0B and $9F
gaps.reason: Defined in the table at $8D9E/$8E9E but no code path found writes these ids and no capture drew them; $09 duplicates the missile $0A, $0B duplicates fan frame $0C, $9F (tiles $CC/$CE) has no known owner. Rendered from an assumed bank, so their look is not proven.

gaps.what: Enemy behaviour types 3 ($AEE1), 27 ($B4F2) and 31 (RTS)
gaps.reason: Never present in any slot type ($030C+i) of any record of any run, nor in the spawn logs (captures/*/spawns.txt); type 3 and 27 handlers reuse generic movement code, so no graphics of their own were found.

gaps.what: Invisible stage-7 controller, type 30 ($B569)
gaps.reason: When the ship is near it rewrites three attribute bytes (block 31: $27D6/$27DE/$27E6 = AF AA FA) and the terrain collision map ($06C2.. from $B612). It belongs to the green barrier of the stage-7 map, which is catalogued only as part of the stage map; its attribute change was not isolated in a capture.

gaps.what: Series names of gr.enemy.row_fighter (type 8), gr.enemy.spinner (types 13/14), gr.enemy.stage3_flyer (type 28), gr.enemy.stage5_roller (type 29)
gaps.reason: Behaviour tracked, but no source ties these NES enemies to a series name. row_fighter behaves like the series Rugal (noted, not asserted). Jumper, Zub, Amoeba, Mother/Child are medium confidence (behaviour + stage match the series descriptions).

gaps.what: Sprite frames without pixel verification
gaps.reason: jumper frames 1/2 and ducker jump in bank 3, hatch ceiling red in bank 3, explosion_large frame from bank 3 (tiles identical to the verified bank-0/2 frames); sprite 0 (always behind the status bar, invisible by design); the three unused metasprites.

gaps.what: CHR bank 1 tile 496 (sprite tile $F0/$F1 top) differs US/JP
gaps.reason: Only metasprite $5E (Rush frame 0) uses tile $F1 and it is never drawn while bank 1 is active, so the difference is never displayed.

gaps.what: Bounding boxes of char-drawn objects (Moai heads, volcanoes, blocks, nucleus, brain)
gaps.reason: These objects are map data with no object table; boxes come from tool heuristics (Moai mouth patterns of $CA29, contiguous terrain runs, non-star bounding box) on the stitched maps. The full maps are in captures/stage_maps/.

gaps.what: Map columns scrolled during the boss phase ($85/$86)
gaps.reason: Excluded to keep the stage-6 nucleus before its erase; the boss arena is empty starfield drawn with bank 2 and BG palettes 2/3 blanked (block 30). Frames are in usA records.

gaps.what: Loop 2+ behaviour differences
gaps.reason: No new metasprite, tile or palette was drawn in loop 2 (usL2) or JP loops 2-6 (jpEnd); code reading $1A (e.g. $B951) changes behaviour only.

gaps.what: Hidden 1UP pick-up
gaps.reason: The pick-up requires an even score digit ($07E5 bit 0); usC forced it even and moved the ship onto the invisible object (documented RAM writes). Natural pick-up not recorded.

gaps.what: ROM check failure texts (KONAMI TEN / GRADIUS TEN)
gaps.reason: The supplied ROMs pass both checks.

gaps.what: Natural stage-skip triggers
gaps.reason: In usB/usL2 the skip was triggered by the Moai counter $5F reaching 10 because the patched invincible ship rammed Moai mouths; the hatch and quick Big Core triggers were read from the code only.

gaps.what: Music and sound effects
gaps.reason: Graphics catalogue only (the project manifest already lists the NSF rips).

gaps.what: types created by other objects (bullets, parts, explosions) are known only from observation
gaps.reason: the static cross-check covers the stage spawn tables ($F338, every type in them was seen in RAM); child spawns go through many call sites ($F655/$F690/$F703) and were not enumerated statically

gaps.what: most enemy names are descriptive (confidence low); Zelos Force (red eye orb) and Crab are unverified series names; Gradius-wiki pages for the FC version list Phoenix, Big Eye, Giga, Crystal Core, Jumping Moai, Big Moai, Big Core MK II, Golem, Tetran, Zelos Force (NES), Covered Core, Crab, Gofer without stage mapping
gaps.reason: no FC Gradius II disassembly/enemy list exists; identity is proven by type id + code, the label is not

gaps.item: Big Core (original) / Death MK II / Demos / Gaw / Intruder / Zub Rush
gaps.what: not present as spawn types
gaps.reason: the boss-rush spawn table (stage 5, 8 sections) contains only $54 Tetran, $57 controller, $58 Covered Core, $5A red orb, $68 Golem, $69 Big Core MK II; no other stage table has a Big Core type. The FC port has no original Big Core boss

gaps.what: stitched full-stage BG maps not built
gaps.reason: out of scope for phase 1; CIRAM/palette dumps every 32 frames with scroll, section ($78/$77) and banks are in captures/stages/ (stages.json nametable_dumps)

gaps.what: work buffers (attribute/collision-like data) saved every 256 frames but not decoded
gaps.reason: not needed for graphics; the PPU state is captured directly

gaps.what: in-game Konami code at pause not tested
gaps.reason: only the title code (UP UP DOWN DOWN LEFT RIGHT LEFT RIGHT B A after skipping the intro -> $07FE=1, 30 lives, $E45A) was tested; no graphics involved

gaps.what: HUD frames are keyed by the meter row; the weapon-set number in their names is the set active when that row was first seen (the meter labels are the same generic SPEED/MISSILE/DOUBLE/LASER/OPTION/? for every set)
gaps.reason: labels are identical across sets

screens.name: Title screen
screens.how_shown: Power-on and after every demo / game over: state $18 = 1 (title init $ED3B, loop $ED60). SELECT toggles 1/2 players ($22), START starts the game; UP UP DOWN DOWN B A on this screen sets $07EF -> 30 lives ($ED5A table, $EED0).
screens.notes: Rev 1 difference: row 27 of the title nametable ($236C-$237C): US reads "LICENSED BY NINTEND OF AMERICA INC." (the RLE literal run has 23 bytes), Rev 1 inserts tile $0C ("O"): "NINTENDO". This one inserted byte at $F4B4 is the only data change between the revisions (see method.md).

screens.name: Attract demo (stages 1, 2, 3 in turn)
screens.how_shown: Title idle ~240 frames -> state $18 = 2 ($EDA4/$F806): $30 = $23 (cycles 0,1,2), recorded input plays the stage; any button returns to the title.
screens.notes: Every sprite seen in the demo maps to the gameplay objects (coverage.json, context demo).

screens.name: Stage start
screens.how_shown: $2C = 0 ($FA0D: CHR loads, palette $FB36, nametable) and 1/2 ($FAC1/$FC02): screen black for ~55 frames, then play starts with the ship flying in ($70 = 2).

screens.name: In-game status bar
screens.how_shown: Every gameplay frame below the sprite-0 split.

screens.name: Pause
screens.how_shown: START during play toggles $24 ($FD81); sound $46.
screens.notes: Rev 1: while paused (and every gameplay frame) the whole palette is re-queued ($FC3F JMP $FCA0 / $FC66 JSR $FCA0 in Rev 1); nothing visible changes in the captures.

screens.name: Game over (status bar text)
screens.how_shown: All players out ($70 = 6): $2C = 5 ($FCEA), "GAME OVER" written in the status bar, play area keeps running ~240 frames.

screens.name: Continue / End
screens.how_shown: After game over while continues remain ($3C, 4 at start -> 3 continues): $2C = 6 ($FD1A). SELECT moves the cursor ($3D), START: CONTINUE restarts the stage, END -> state 6 -> title.

screens.name: Stage clear fly-out
screens.how_shown: Boss destroyed: $4E set, ship state 7 ($C465) flies off, $2C = 4 ($FC9A) -> next stage.

screens.name: Ending: the planet is destroyed
screens.how_shown: After stage 6: $2C = 7 ($FD50: CHR X=$14 and X=$16, bank 1 $AEB7) then 8 ($FD61, bank 1 $AF1B): planet with explosions, the ship flies away, a beam crosses the planet, white flash, planet blast; then the KONAMI screen. If $07DF < 3 after stage 6 the game goes back to stage 4 instead ($FCC9).
screens.notes: No staff roll in this version.

screens.name: Ending: KONAMI screen

gaps.reason: The longer laser segments (ids 9F-A5, from $CB6A) never appeared: the beam was always cut by hits. Layouts are decoded from the metasprite tables (frames marked "static only"), tiles are the same tile $0E as the seen ids, but they are not pixel-verified.

Two-player runs only cover stages 1 and 2. The other stages use the same common sprite streams (X=2 horizontal / X=4 vertical, identical bytes) and the same metasprite entries, so the frames are proven statically, not by capture.
Deaths captured in stages 1 and 2 (unpatched runs deaths1/deaths2) and in the attract demo; same tables/CHR in the other stages.
$90 = 2 (option without owner, overlay alternating 00/09 at $C7C5) never occurred in the captures (no death while carrying options).
Both capsules were captured on screen, but their pickup effects (extra life $D207, screen clear $DAC7) are proven from the code only.
Type 0 with $0483 = 3 uses metasprite id 01 whose common entry draws nothing; listed without frames.
Seen only in 4 lag frames (renderer skipped, slot/OAM pairing impossible); never on a verifiable frame.

Every enemy object is proven by its type byte $03FB and the ids its slot showed; the names are labels given by looking at the frames and the logged behaviour (confidence medium/low). series_name is left null; the Data Crystal / wiki pages could not be fetched (request blocked: https://datacrystal.tcrf.net/wiki/Life_Force), so no series name was verified.

Bosses are catalogued by stage (lf.s1.boss .. lf.s6.boss) with the brief's names in lead_name only: brain with tentacles (stage 1, lead Golem), mechanical core with ball arms (stage 2, lead Tetran), fire dragon (stage 3, lead Intruder), giant skull (stage 4), pharaoh head (stage 5), red sphere (stage 6, final). No object matching "Crystal Core" was found in the six stages; "Zelos/Giga" could not be attached to a specific boss with evidence.

Destructible/regenerating cell walls (stage 1), rock blocks (stage 2), base gun emplacements (stage 2), prominence arcs (stage 3), nerve-cell tentacles and rib cage (stage 4), golden statue and temple walls (stage 5), barriers (stage 6) are background: they are in the nametable dumps and stitched stage maps, but not split into separate layout-matrix objects. Their sprite parts (invisible hit boxes, explosions) are catalogued (lf.s1.wall_cell_block, lf.s2.rock_block, lf.s2.base_turret, lf.s5.temple_block, lf.s6.barrier).
The masked CHR rewrite (bank 6 $8D91, source pointers $8E44) is captured frame by frame (captures/s1a/chrr) but its source table was not decoded statically.

Built from nametable dumps every 8 frames, each cell drawn with the CHR/palette of its dump; looping sections (stage 2 base, $6D) appear once; maps are not pixel-compared with screenshots (individual state dumps are).
After the ending the game restarts at stage 1 with $31 = 1; same graphics (same loads), only the first part of loop 2 stage 1 was captured (end6).

Frames whose evidence OAM entries scored < 0.8 (sprites behind the background, palette-cycling overlays, flicker): lf.item.capsule_blue id 08 ov 04; lf.item.capsule_blue id 0A ov 04; lf.s2.base_sphere id 55 ov 01; lf.s2.wall_cannon id C8; lf.s2.wall_cannon id CE; lf.s2.needle_shot id D5; lf.s2.needle_shot id D5 ov 01; lf.s2.needle_shot id DA ov 01; lf.s2.pod_drone id E3 ov 01; lf.s4.pink_pod id A9 ov 01; lf.s6.boss_spawn id B2; lf.s6.color_orb id A7 ov 25; lf.s6.color_orb id A7 ov 28; lf.s6.color_orb id A7 ov 29; lf.s6.color_orb id A7 ov 2B; lf.s6.color_orb id A7 ov 2C; lf.s6.color_orb id A7 ov 2D; lf.s6.color_orb id A7 ov 2F; lf.s6.color_orb id A7 ov 30; lf.ending.vic_viper_flyaway id D8 ov 04

gaps.what: Stage map (metatile index sequences) and the static source of the background-drawn bosses
gaps.reason: Not decoded. Backgrounds are drawn by the metatile writer $E01C from WRAM $6800+ (4x4-tile metatiles, queue mode 5); the map stream that feeds it was not traced. Stage pictures are stitched from the captured nametables (captures/stageN_bg_stitched.png, captures/sN/nt.npz every 4 frames) and the WRAM after init is dumped (captures/sN/wram_after_init_*.bin). Boss tile matrices are the captured nametables; no RLE stream in PRG matches them (scan of 139 nametable RLE streams).

gaps.what: Exact extent of the background-drawn destructible targets (type 8, S2 $1C/$2A/$2E, S4 $4A, S5 $51, S6 $56)
gaps.reason: They draw no sprite; the catalogue gives a 7x7-tile nametable window centred on the hit-box position just before destruction (confidence medium). The hit-box size table ($0507 & $0F -> $CF97) was not decoded into tile extents.

gaps.what: Names of all enemy, boss and scenery objects
gaps.reason: Descriptive labels chosen by looking (name_confidence low); series_name left null for every enemy/boss. The web pages that could give series names (tcrf.net/Salamander_(NES), gradius.fandom.com/wiki/Salamander_(Famicom)) were blocked (permission not granted). Identity (type byte, state table, sprite ids) is code-proven.

gaps.what: Loops 2 and 3 ($31 = 1, 2)
gaps.reason: Only the start of loop 2 was captured (run ending). The sprite tables are indexed by $30 only, so graphics are the same; possible behaviour differences that read $31 (e.g. bank6 $AE6C copies $31 into an object variable) were not catalogued.

gaps.what: Item kind 3 (bonus score, $0529 = 3)
gaps.reason: Never spawned in the captures; invisible by code (sprite id 1 is empty, $DA68). Catalogued from code only (sfc.item.bonus, confidence medium).

gaps.what: Pick-up of a loose option by the other player
gaps.reason: Loose options ($80,X = 2) were captured (runs d1/d2) and are catalogued; the pick-up itself was not separately verified.

gaps.what: Stage-1 boss CHR materialisation (43 BG tiles rewritten bit by bit, frames 13152-13855)
gaps.reason: Documented by code (bank6 $8E40, queue mode 4) and by the CHR images in captures/s1/chr.npz (one per changed frame); the intermediate tile states are not catalogued as separate frames.

gaps.what: Letter-by-letter mapping of the title and HUD fonts
gaps.reason: Digits are code-proven ($EC + n); letters are only known through the strings that use them (sfc.font.title / sfc.font.hud).

gaps.what: OAM at mode switches
gaps.reason: 59 frames in total are not reproduced by the composer model: 16 (run title) and 35 (run g1) around demo start/end where the title OAM writer and the composer overlap, 2 at game over -> continue (run d2) and 6 at ending -> loop 2 (run ending), all screen transitions with several skipped NMIs; also the first 4 frames of the run started from a savestate (ending) have no RAM history. Coverage lists them; no unknown sprite appears there.

gaps.what: Invincibility-blink variants of every posture
gaps.reason: The blink forces the palette (attr modifier 5 for P1, 4 for P2, $C39A); not every posture x orientation x player combination happened while blinking (e.g. P2 horizontal $82 with attr 4). They are the same tiles with the palette forced, derivable from the frames given.

gaps.what: Sound effects and music
gaps.reason: Out of scope of this graphics catalogue (sound ids are quoted in code_refs only).
